clue.text: Father to the French and German lady

parts.note: FR is the standard abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
in French 'to the' (masculine) is au

explanation.surface: A priest goes off to France with a woman from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German word for a married woman, the title equivalent to Mrs.

clue.text: Call and get back a bit of music on the line — it gets under your skin

parts.note: to call someone on the phone is to ring them

indicators.note: get back tells us the pieces that follow are read in the opposite direction
on places one piece directly before the other in the run

parts.note: M is the first bit of the word music
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A phone call brings back a snatch of melody down the line, and it irritates you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get back' turns M placed on ROW (MROW) into WORM.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal infection lives in the skin, a playful take on the idiom for something irritating.

clue.text: Head, not heart, missing — it's obvious

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head, especially its crown

indicators.note: heart missing says the centre letter of the word not is removed

explanation.surface: Someone with a brain but no compassion is plainly evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain or evident, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: Demos in favour of SATs?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
SATs are standardised school tests, in Britain taken by primary pupils

explanation.surface: Is a street march really a show of support for school exams?
explanation.definitionFit: Demos is short for demonstrations, public marches or rallies of objection.

clue.text: Traveller broadcasting from resort?

parts.note: a rep (sales representative) is a commercial traveller
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A tourist sending out radio reports from a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, but it is the verb: to resort to somewhere is to go there.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to go or betake oneself to a place, as in repairing to the bar.

clue.text: Rental reportedly increased

indicators.note: reportedly says a word is to be heard rather than spelt as written

parts.note: something increased is higher

explanation.surface: Word has it that the rent has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire, as a noun, is the act of renting something, or the fee paid for it.

clue.text: Worker finds working a strain

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A labourer discovers that doing the job is tiring.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a craftsman.

clue.text: Diana, a leading royal, having awkward times

indicators.note: leading takes just the opening letter of the word royal
awkward suggests the letters of the word times are in an ungainly order

explanation.surface: Princess Diana, a senior royal, going through difficult periods.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Princess of Wales; the Roman goddess Diana was the counterpart of the Greek huntress.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of the hunt, identified by the Romans with their Diana.

clue.text: One stops a bribe

definitions.meaning: a stopper for a cask or hole, something that plugs it
British slang for a payment made to buy favour

explanation.surface: A man halts a backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a stopper for a cask, and in British slang also a bribe or illicit payment.

clue.text: One stationed abroad has no right to talk about something

indicators.note: has no says a letter is missing from the longer word

parts.note: an expatriate is someone living outside their own country

explanation.surface: A person posted overseas has no right to comment.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject.

clue.text: Drunk hit copper with knowledge of likely outcome

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into disorder

explanation.surface: An intoxicated man struck a policeman, as anyone could have foreseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophetic means foretelling events, seeing what is to come.

clue.text: Hit nail on the head of clumsy oaf

indicators.note: on the head of picks the opening letter of the word clumsy

parts.note: a lout is an uncouth oaf

explanation.surface: Strike the nail on the head, you clumsy fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius gives two definitions, a blow and a short flat-headed nail, plus wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy blow, and a clout nail is a short nail with a large flat head.

clue.text: Officers take a drink

parts.note: two COs, commanding officers

explanation.surface: Servicemen of rank have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: With expired email provider one needs paper

parts.note: ob, short for Latin obiit, means died
a mail server delivers email

explanation.surface: Someone whose email account has lapsed needs a newspaper instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observer is a long-running British Sunday newspaper, so a paper.

clue.text: Latter part of month can be hot

indicators.note: latter part of says only the closing letters of the month's name are kept

parts.note: September, among other months, ends in the needed letters

explanation.surface: The end of the month can be warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The month could equally be November or December; all end the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing piece of coal or wood that stays hot after a fire.

clue.text: Burgers rejected a cheat

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Macs, as in Big Macs, are burgers

explanation.surface: Turning down burgers is a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or fraudulent trick.

clue.text: Distinctive character makes some get hostile

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Having a strong personality makes some people turn aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a person or group.

clue.text: Happening to die oddly late in the day

parts.note: an event is a happening

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of the word die are in a strange order

explanation.surface: An occurrence where someone passes away strangely in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Test this for difficult multiplication?

parts.note: the surface suggests hard arithmetic, but the multiplication is reproduction

explanation.surface: Try this method on a tricky multiplication sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is used in IVF, the laboratory method for couples who find conceiving hard.

clue.text: End of semester?

parts.note: a playful reading: the close of a semester is the end of term, and the word means an end point

explanation.surface: The close of the academic half-year.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is an end point, and the word contains term, the close of which ends a semester.

clue.text: Window as in Bond

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: cement is a binding material, a bond

explanation.surface: A window as seen in a James Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side so it opens like a door.

clue.text: Birds, for example,disturbed rest

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of the word rest are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Birds, for instance, upset by someone's sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons of marshes and shores.

clue.text: It's a mistake to lose head in fright

indicators.note: lose head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: terror is great fright

explanation.surface: Panicking and losing your nerve when scared is a bad idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an error is a blunder or slip, the same as a mistake.

clue.text: City den for a comedienne

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London
a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A London den that is home to a female comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Eclair is a British stand-up comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenny Eclair is a well-known British stand-up comedienne, so the surname names one.

clue.text: It's rejected in present state of conventional wisdom

definitions.text: It's rejected in present state of conventional wisdom

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the run made by the other two

parts.note: here means present, in attendance
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Something repudiated by today's accepted thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal on the word It's, and 'in' puts the turned piece between the other two; read straight, the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretical view is one rejected as contrary to accepted belief or orthodoxy.

clue.text: One among the Irish who stands to gain from a death

definitions.text: who stands to gain from a death

indicators.note: among says the answer lies within the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An Irishman set to benefit from someone dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir inherits property when its owner dies.

clue.text: Composer yields not a note

indicators.note: not says the named letter is left out

parts.note: gives means yields, as ground gives under pressure
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A composer gives way, without a single note.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a twentieth-century American composer.

clue.text: Six is a point off seven

indicators.note: off says the named letter is taken away

parts.note: S is a compass point, south

explanation.surface: Six is just one notch short of seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes a sentence: six is divisible by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Six is a number divisible by two, an even number.

clue.text: Bird causes a measure of trouble

parts.note: a pint is a measure of liquid
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A bird stirs up a lot of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Pintado is a name for the guinea fowl and for the Cape petrel.

clue.text: Weapon almost goes off without reasons

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a gun goes off when it fires

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A gun that nearly discharges without cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'almost' trims the weapon to its first two letters before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to reckon or reason out, as in he figures it will rain.
